facts.fact: La Sentinelle reports that Algeria's national all-fibre strategy aims to generalise FTTH across the whole territory by 2027, with the copper network phased out by the same date; the document gives no period that has ended and names no successor, and the strategy's adoption date is not stated (reported 2026-10-01, ministry communique of 2026-09-30).

note: Ministerial order setting the tender calendar for universal-service mobile coverage of 3,000 low-density localities; a universal service tender with no national broadband plan named, so other.
ARPCE universal-service mobile coverage tender for 3,000 areas; no national broadband plan named, so other.
Minister states copper replacement by fibre by end 2026 or early 2027 and subscriber figures, but names no plan or strategy and sets no figures against plan targets.

facts.fact: TechAfrica News reports Minister Zerrouki said in a 20 February 2026 video message that the government has adopted a comprehensive all-fibre communications strategy to extend high-speed infrastructure nationwide; no adoption date or period is given, so the date is the message date.

The Ministry of Post and Telecommunications said on 2026-02-17 that 3 million households have FTTH and that this is part of its "Tout Fibre" strategy, which aims to generalise fibre by 2027 at the latest, so the plan's period had not ended.

note: Minister's statement on international bandwidth and cables; names no broadband plan, only a fibre completion date of Q2 2027 and the ministry's action plan.

facts.fact: The Minister told the ITU WTDC-25 on 2025-11-18 that the government is implementing an infrastructure agenda of nationwide fibre expansion aiming for full coverage by 2027, with over 1,500 villages connected and 3,000 to go through universal service programmes, so the period had not ended.

note: Launch of the Medusa submarine cable project; a single project, not a national broadband plan.

facts.fact: The Ministry's page of 2025-07-09 sets the sector's strategic goal of 7 million households on fixed internet by the end of 2027, with FTTH as the core technology, so the period had not ended.

The Ministry reports 6.6 million fixed internet subscribers in the first half of 2025, up from 3.5 million in early 2020, against its goal of 7 million households by end-2027, and says the intermediate objectives were reached.
